adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — [confidence 100; P1; blocking] `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` uses Redis's default SUM aggregation, so replaying a child after its parent buffer has merged adds its timestamp to the existing score and makes eviction retain that older duplicate while deleting genuinely newer spans instead.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that zunionstore with default SUM aggregation will add scores together when the same member exists in multiple sets. Looking at the diff, spans are stored with their end_timestamp_precise as the score (line 196-198 in buffer.py shows `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})`). When zunionstore merges sets containing the same span payload, the timestamps will be summed rather than taking the max or min. This corrupts the ordering, and when zpopmin is called to evict spans exceeding the 1000 limit (lines 57-58 in add-buffer.lua), it will evict based on incorrect scores. A span that was replayed would have an artificially high score (sum of timestamps) and would be retained while genuinely newer spans with correct single timestamps would be evicted. This is a real correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — [confidence 100; P2; blocking] `for i = 0, 1000 do` stops before the root of a redirect chain longer than 1001 links, so a late child under the oldest ancestor is inserted and flushed under an intermediate segment ID instead of joining its existing root segment, because evicting payloads does not shorten the redirect chain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that reducing the loop limit from 10000 to 1000 will cause issues with redirect chains longer than 1001 links. However, looking at the diff, the loop limit change is accompanied by a new span count limit that caps spans at 1000 (via zpopmin). The system is designed to handle at most 1000 spans per segment, so having redirect chains longer than 1000 would be inconsistent with the new design. The redirect chain depth corresponds to the tree depth of spans, and with a maximum of 1000 spans, having a chain depth exceeding 1000 would require a degenerate linear chain which is bounded by the span limit. The finding misunderstands the relationship between the redirect chain limit and the span count limit - they are being aligned together.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in buffer.py, the code that checked `max_segment_spans` and enforced the limit was removed (lines 446-453 deleted). Meanwhile, in add-buffer.lua, a hardcoded limit of 1000 is introduced (line 63: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`). The SpansBuffer class still accepts `max_segment_spans` as a constructor parameter (visible in the existing code structure), but this Lua script enforces a fixed 1000 limit regardless of what value is configured. This creates a disconnect where the configurable parameter is ignored and a hardcoded value is used instead, which is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:434 — [confidence 100; P1; blocking] Replacing SSCAN with `p.zscan(key, cursor=cursor, count=self.segment_page_size)` and SADD with `p.zadd(` at line 197 while retaining the existing `span-buf:s:` key namespace makes upgraded workers raise Redis WRONGTYPE on pre-deployment SET buffers, blocking flushes and inserts until those buffered spans expire, while rollback workers likewise reject newly written sorted sets because the change provides no compatible reader, conversion, or drain transition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis SET operations (SADD, SSCAN, SCARD) to SORTED SET operations (ZADD, ZSCAN, ZCARD) in both buffer.py and add-buffer.lua, while using the same key namespace 'span-buf:s:'. In buffer.py line 197, SADD is replaced with ZADD, and in line 434, SSCAN is replaced with ZSCAN. The Lua script similarly changes from 'scard'/'sunionstore' to 'zcard'/'zunionstore'. During deployment, if old workers have written SET data with these keys, new workers calling ZSCAN/ZADD on those keys will get WRONGTYPE errors from Redis. Similarly, during rollback, old workers calling SSCAN/SADD on sorted set keys will fail. There's no migration, conversion, or dual-read logic to handle this transition, making this a real deployment/rollback compatibility bug.
